items.headline: Tyler Higbee (chest) listed as questionable
items.news: Higbee has been diagnosed with a pulmonary contusion that he sustained in the Rams' 26-13 win over the Packers in Week 12, and his status for Week 13 against the Chiefs on Thursday, Dec. 3 won't be known until Wednesday, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
items.analysis: Higbee is considered week-to-week, and his status for Thursday's game won't be known until the Rams resume practicing during Week 13 prep. The Rams are already expected to be without Davis Allen (ankle) for multiple weeks, and the absence of Higbee would leave Colby Parkinson and Max Klare as the team's top options at tight end against Kansas City.

items.headline: Davante Adams (hamstring) nearing return from IR
items.news: The Rams are not expected to open the 21-day practice window for Adams (hamstring) ahead of the team's Week 13 game against the Chiefs, Nate Adkins of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: Head coach Sean McVay told reporters Saturday that Adams hasn't suffered a setback in his recovery from a hamstring injury, but the veteran wide receiver has not progressed enough to be cleared to return to practice, per Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site. With Adams out for at least one more game, his next opportunity to take the field will be Week 14 against the 49ers on Sunday, Dec. 13. In the absence of both Adams and Puka Nacua (knee, IR), the Rams' top wide receivers for Week 13 will be Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith.

items.headline: Noah Fant (calf) listed as questionable
items.news: Fant (calf) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Bengals, while Juwan Johnson (hamstring) has been ruled out, Matthew Paras of the New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
items.analysis: Fant would be in line to operate as the top TE for the Saints if he gets the green light to suit up against the team for which he played last season. The 29-year-old Fant has scored either three or four touchdowns in six of his eight NFL regular seasons, including three apiece in 2025 with Cincinnati and so far in 2026 with New Orleans. Rookie third-round pick Oscar Delp is the next tight end up if Fant joins Johnson on the sidelines.

items.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) injury update
items.news: Burks (foot) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Arizona.
items.analysis: Burks opened Week 12 prep with back-to-back limited listings due to a lingering foot injury, but a full practice Friday has him in the clear ahead of the weekend. In three appearances since Week 8 while playing with the issue, he's combined for a 7-138-0 line on 11 targets during that span.

items.headline: Stefon Diggs (personal) injury update
items.news: Diggs (personal) was removed from the Commanders' injury report Thursday.
items.analysis: Diggs had an excused absence Wednesday but avoided the injury report entirely one day later, setting him up to continue to serve as Washington's clear-cut No. 1 wide receiver. Since Terry McLaurin was lost for the season due to a torn patellar tendon that he suffered in Week 6 at San Francisco, Diggs has compiled a 16-217-2 line on 27 targets over the last four games.

items.headline: Jalen McMillan (knee/calf) nearing return from IR
items.news: McMillan (knee/calf) is practicing Saturday, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
items.analysis: McMillan was listed as a full participant on Thursday's estimated practice report before having his reps limited during Friday's session. The third-year wide receiver has been on injured reserve since suffering an MCL sprain in Week 3, and he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Monday's NFC South showdown against the Panthers. Given his extended absence, McMillan would likely operate as the Buccaneers' WR4 in his potential return behind Chris Godwin, Emeka Egbuka and rookie third-rounder Ted Hurst.

items.headline: Caleb Williams (abdomen) listed as questionable
items.news: Williams said after Thursday's 39-35 win in Detroit that he's "fine" and likely just has "a bruise on his abdomen," Jason Lieser of the Chicago Sun-Times reports.
items.analysis: Williams seemingly went for a precautionary X-ray after Week 12 action due to a "weird fall" that occurred during Thursday's contest in which he engineered two TD drives in the final 8:20 of the fourth quarter to eke out a four-point victory. He completed 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and recorded three carries for 15 yards. With plenty of time to recover before the Bears' next game Sunday, Dec. 6 against the Jaguars, Williams has a decent chance to avoid practice restrictions next week.

items.headline: Woody Marks (concussion) injury update
items.news: Marks (concussion) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Marks, who was inactive Nov. 19 against the Colts, logged 'full' listings at practice Wednesday through Friday and now has gained clearance to rejoin the lineup after being sidelined for one game. His Week 11 absence coincided with the return to action of fellow RB David Montgomery, and now that both backs are available for the first time since Week 5, look for Marks to see a noticeable dip in volume while sharing touches with Montgomery, who logged 26 carries versus Indianapolis.

items.headline: Dalton Schultz (illness) injury update
items.news: Schultz (illness) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Schultz practiced without limitations Friday, shedding any doubts about his availability after an illness limited his participation Thursday. The Ravens have allowed seven TDs to TEs this season, which is seventh most in the NFL, but Schultz has scored only once all season and is coming off consecutive one-catch performances.

items.headline: Denzel Boston (quadriceps) listed as questionable
items.news: Boston (quadriceps) wasn't present for Friday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of the Cleveland Plain Dealerreports.
items.analysis: With Boston now on track to log a trio of 'DNP' listings this week, his status for Sunday night's game against the Raiders is cloudy. Friday's final injury report will reveal whether the Browns' starting WR has any chance to play versus Las Vegas or is ruled out ahead of Week 12 action.

items.headline: Brock Purdy (ankle) ruled out
items.news: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Friday that Purdy (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game versus the Seahawks, Jennifer Lee Chan of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.analysis: Purdy wasn't able to practice during Week 12 prep due to an ankle injury, which will sideline him for the first time this season. In place of Purdy, Mac Jones will earn the spot start Sunday, while the former's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 6, at the Giants. Shanahan added that surgery isn't on the table for Purdy and he's optimistic the QB will be OK to return in Week 13, according to Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com.

items.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) injury update
items.news: Smith-Njigba (ankle) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest in San Francisco, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.
items.analysis: The Seahawks listed Smith-Njigba as limited on the first two Week 12 injury reports due to an ankle issue, but he'll play through it in Sunday's NFC West showdown. In the first matchup with the 49ers back in Week 5, he hauled in five of eight targets for 102 yards and one touchdown.

items.headline: Sam Darnold (quadriceps) injury update
items.news: Darnold (quadriceps) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at San Francisco, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.
items.analysis: Darnold thus is returning from a two-game absence due to a quad injury and cracked ribs, benefiting from the Seahawks' Week 11 bye. When asked if Darnold is 100 percent, head coach Mike Macdonald told Bell that "pretty much nobody is fully health at this point in the season," indicating that the quarterback still may be dealing with residual effects of those health concerns. In any case, Darnold will resume starting duties for the Seahawks this weekend.

items.headline: Brenen Thompson (hamstring) listed as doubtful
items.news: Thompson (hamstring) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Patriots, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports.
items.analysis: Thompson has not played since Week 2 against the Raiders due to a hamstring injury, and it looks like that trend will continue after the rookie fourth-rounder missed all three practices during Week 12 prep. Assuming he doesn't play Sunday, Thompson's next opportunity to play would be Week 13 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 6.

items.headline: Hunter Long (ankle) listed as questionable
items.news: Long (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Commanders, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
items.analysis: The tight end returned from injured reserve two weeks ago and has two grabs for 18 yards on three targets in two games since suffering a knee injury. Long is now dealing with an ankle issue. Teagan Quitoriano would see an uptick in snaps behind Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins if Long is unable to play.

items.headline: Jared Wayne (quadriceps) ruled out
items.news: Wayne (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets.
items.analysis: Wayne will end up missing a third consecutive game due to a quadriceps injury, and his next chance to suit up is Week 13 against the Broncos on Sunday, Dec. 6. Kevin Coleman and Jalen Tolbert will continue to operate in slightly expanded roles on offense in Wayne's absence.

items.headline: Reggie Gilliam (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Gilliam (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
items.analysis: Gilliam returned from injured reserve in Week 10 against the Lions and is now coming off the bye week, but he's still dealing with the knee issue. The fullback has touched the ball two times on offense this season, logging 71 snaps and another 56 on special teams.

items.headline: Brevin Jordan (foot) ruled out
items.news: Jordan (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
items.analysis: The tight end logged a trio of DNPs this week and will miss a third straight contest. With Jordan remaining sidelined, Dalton Schultz, Foster Moreau, Marlin Klein and Cade Stover will be the healthy options at the position for Houston. Jordan has two catches for 12 yards on two targets across five contests this season.

items.headline: Drew Ogletree (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Ogletree (knee) is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game versus the Giants.
items.analysis: Ogletree sat out practice Friday after logging a full session Thursday, casting doubt back onto his availability for Week 12. If he can't play Sunday, it would likely mean increased snaps at tight end for veteran Pharaoh Brown.

items.headline: Tez Johnson (illness) listed as questionable
items.news: Johnson did not participate in Friday's practice due to an illness.
items.analysis: Johnson wasn't listed on Thursday's practice report, so the illness is a recent development for the second-year wide receiver. His participation level, if any, in Saturday's practice will provide clarity on his status heading into Monday's game against the Panthers.

items.headline: Feleipe Franks (wrist) listed as questionable
items.news: Franks (wrist) was a limited participant at practice Friday.
items.analysis: Franks popped up on the Panthers' injury report with a wrist injury Thursday, and now there's a cloud over his status for Week 12. He may end up taking an injury designation into game day if he's not able to upgrade to full participation at practice Saturday.

items.headline: Will Mallory (hamstring) ruled out
items.news: Mallory (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants.
items.analysis: Mallory is set to miss a fourth consecutive game due to a hamstring injury. The Colts are on bye for Week 13, so his next opportunity to play is Week 14 against the Eagles on Sunday, Dec. 13. Drew Ogletree (knee) is listed as questionable after stringing together a DNP-FP-DNP practice log, and if he cannot play Sunday, then Pharaoh Brown would serve as the Colts' TE2 behind Tyler Warren.

items.headline: Jordan Watkins (groin) ruled out
items.news: Watkins (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Warkins was held out of practice all week due to a groin injury, and the second-year wide receiver will end up missing his third game of the season and first since Week 2 against the Dolphins. Keenan Allen, Jacob Cowing and Demarcus Robinson are all candidates for more offensive snaps Sunday in the absence of Watkins, whose next chance to play is Week 13 against the Giants on Sunday, Dec. 6.

items.headline: Mike Evans (achilles) listed as questionable
items.news: Evans (Achilles) is listed as questionable for Sunday's contest against the Seahawks, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.analysis: Evans didn't practice Wednesday before he was listed as limited on Thursday's injury report as he continues to deal with the right Achilles tendinitis that forced him out of a Week 6 matchup with the Commanders. He returned to action this past Sunday versus the Vikings in Mexico City and gathered in six of seven targets for 109 yards and one touchdown on a 43 percent snap share. Evans' status will be clarified about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.

items.headline: Drew Lock (elbow) injury update
items.news: Lock (elbow) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Lock started in each of the Seahawks' two games prior to the Week 11 bye in the absence of Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs), and the former has been working through a right elbow injury over the past month. However, Lock's lack of an injury tag for Week 12 means he'll be available to serve as the Seahawks' backup to Darnold on Sunday while Jalen Milroe (illness) serves as the emergency third quarterback.

items.headline: Justin Herbert (concussion) ruled out
items.news: Herbert (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
items.analysis: At 1-9, the Chargers have zero incentive to rush Herbert back to the field at this stage. His next chance to see game action thus is slated to arrive Sunday, Dec. 6, against the Buccaneers. In Herbet's absence this weekend, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network relays that DJ Uiagalelei is slated to start at QB for the Chargers, with Jake Browning available to back him up.

items.headline: Keaton Mitchell (knee) ruled out
items.news: Mitchell (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Mitchell tweaked his knee during the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets in Week 11. The injury prevented the fourth-year pro from practicing all week, and his absence for Sunday's contest means Kimani Vidal should operate in an expanded role in the backfield behind RB1 Omarion Hampton. Mitchell's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 6.

items.headline: David Njoku (shoulder) listed as questionable
items.news: Njoku (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against New England.
items.analysis: Njoku was held out of practice both Wednesday and Thursday due to a shoulder injury that he sustained during the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets. He was cleared to return to practice in a limited capacity Friday, which was enough for the veteran tight end to draw the questionable tag for Sunday's contest. Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will maintain expanded roles on offense in the event that Njoku doesn't play, and Patrick Herbert would be a candidate for elevation from the practice squad to give the Chargers more depth at tight end. That said, the Chargers' offensive potential figures to be limited in Week 12 in the absence of Justin Herbert (concussion), with DJ Uiagalelei set to make his first career start.

items.headline: Brock Bowers (ankle) listed as questionable
items.news: Bowers (ankle) will be listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against the Browns, Adam Hill of the Las Vegas Review-Journal reports.
items.analysis: Per Sam Warren of The Athletic, Bowers didn't practice Friday after being limited the previous two days. It's unclear if the star TE's 'DNP' to close the week was maintenance or setback related, but the Raiders' late kickoff presents an issue for those considering Bowers in Week 12 fantasy lineups. As one of the marquee names carrying a 'questionable' tag into the weekend, look for added context regarding his status to arrive no later than Saturday night or Sunday morning via the usual notable NFL insiders.

items.headline: Isaiah Williams (ribs) injury update
items.news: Williams (ribs) practiced fully Thursday, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Williams -- who was inactive in Week 11-- was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's estimated practice report, but his full participation a day later paves the way for him to return to action Sunday against the Dolphins. With fellow wideout Omar Cooper (ankle/groin) in danger of missing his second straight game, Williams could end up working as the Jets' WR3 this weekend behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell in the event that he's active and Cooper isn't.

items.headline: Darren Waller (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Waller (knee) practiced in a limited fashion Friday.
items.analysis: Waller was among four Panthers tight ends to have a capped session Friday, the others being Tommy Tremble (knee), Mitchell Evans (Achilles) and Feleipe Franks (wrist). Waller was able to play through his knee injury this past Sunday against the Ravens, when he handled a 46 percent snap share en route to three catches (on three targets) for 42 yards.

items.headline: Tetairoa McMillan (foot) listed as questionable
items.news: McMillan (foot) was not in uniform for the team stretch portion of Friday's practice, but he did suit up afterward, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reported earlier Friday that McMillan was in a helmet and pads, and although he ditched them while stretching he put them back on shortly afterward. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will include McMillan's activity level, if any, after he was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's practice estimate due to a sore foot.

items.headline: Myles Price (knee/groin) injury update
items.news: Price (knee/groin) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Emily Leiker of the Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
items.analysis: Price was limited at practice Wednesday and Thursday but upgraded to full participation Friday and has been cleared to suit up. He, along with Tai Felton and Jauan Jennings, will vie for larger roles alongside Justin Jefferson as the Vikings continue to play without Jordan Addison (thumb) against Atlanta's mediocre secondary.

items.headline: Isaiah Likely (groin) injury update
items.news: Likely (groin) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest at Indianapolis, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
items.analysis: Likely was listed as limited on the injury report Wednesday and Thursday due to the groin strain that he picked up in practice last Friday, but it won't keep him from suiting up again in Week 12. While playing through the issue this past Sunday against the Jaguars, he took on a normal 76 percent snap share but recorded just one catch (on three targets) for 35 yards.

items.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) injury update
items.news: Meyers (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Ryan O'Halloran of the Florida Times-Union reports.
items.analysis: Meyers has managed to shake off an ankle injury that limited his practice participation earlier in the week. He racked up a season-high 85 yards on 10 targets in Jacksonville's Week 11 loss to the Giants, and Meyers is likely to get plenty of attention from Trevor Lawrence against Tennessee's league-worst secondary Sunday in the absence of top Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington (shoulder), giving Meyers appealing upside in nearly all fantasy formats.

items.headline: Rashod Bateman (groin) practice update
items.news: Bateman (groin) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com reports.
items.analysis: Bateman was limited in Wednesday's session due to a groin injury, but his full practice Thursday puts the sixth-year wide receiver on track to play against the Texans on Sunday. He hauled in his second touchdown of the year in a Week 11 loss to the Panthers and is up to a 25-403-2 receiving line on 42 targets through 11 regular-season games.

items.headline: Zay Flowers (ankle) practice update
items.news: Flowers (ankle) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice.
items.analysis: Flowers was limited at practice Wednesday, but the wide receiver's quick return to all activity one day later clears the way for him to suit up Sunday against the Texans. In his last outing, Flowers (who has recorded a fantasy-friendly 57-785-3 line on 82 targets through 10 games), was on the field for 88 percent of his team's snaps on offense in a 35-33 loss to the Panthers in Week 11 en route to catching eight of his game-high 11 targets for 97 yards.

items.headline: Derrick Henry (concussion) injury update
items.news: Henry (concussion) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Texans, per Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio.
items.analysis: Henry has cleared concussion protocol after practicing without limitations Thursday and Friday. He'll try to help the Ravens snap a six-game losing streak Sunday against the Texans. Running room could be hard to come by against a stout Houston front that's allowing fewer than 100 rushing yards per game, though Henry has overcome more than his fair share of daunting matchups over the years.

items.headline: Kayshon Boutte (hip) ruled out
items.news: Boutte (hip) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Boutte's absence will coincide with the return of Marvin Harrison (hamstring) from a two-game absence. Harrison will join Nico Collins, Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson while Boutte sits out due to an hip injury the latter sustained in last Thursday's win over the Colts, which subsequently prevented Boutte from practicing in any capacity during Week 12 prep. Boutte's next chance to take the field will be Sunday, Dec. 6, at Pittsburgh.

items.headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) injury update
items.news: Murray (hamstring) doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Falcons, Emily Leiker of the Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
items.analysis: Murray has been cleared to suit up for the first time since Week 8 after practicing without limitations Friday. He's set to back up Kirk Cousins, who is entrenched as Minnesota's starting QB after being reacquired in a trade with the Raiders.

items.headline: Raheim Sanders (hip) nearing return from IR
items.news: Sanders (hip) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Mary Kay Cabot of the Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
items.analysis: Sanders was designated to return from injured reserve Tuesday, and he would need to be added to the active roster with an official transaction prior to Sunday's game to have a chance to play. Even if Sanders gets the green light, he's unlikely to see much action on offense, with Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson and Jaleel McLaughlin all healthy in Cleveland's backfield.

items.headline: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) nearing return from IR
items.news: Iosivas (thumb) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints.
items.analysis: Iosivas had his 21-day window to return from IR opened Nov. 12, so the Bengals are running out of time to add him back to the active roster before he would need to miss the remainder of the season. If Iosivas isn't activated ahead of Sunday's game, expect such a move to transpire early the following week before the Bengals travel to Cleveland. Dohnte Meyers has been filling in as Cincinnati's No. 3 WR during Iosivas' ongoing absence.

items.headline: Tee Higgins (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: After not practicing Friday, Higgins (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Higgins wasn't on the Bengals' Week 12 injury report until Friday, but after missing the team's final practice, the wideout's status is now worth tracking ahead of Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. While a late-week downgrade in practice participation like this can't be ignored, Ben Baby of ESPN.com notes that "Higgins just woke up with some soreness" Friday and that the team gave the WR "the day to work through it." More importantly, Baby indicates that the issue isn't a concern in terms of Higgins' availability versus New Orleans.

items.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) ruled out
items.news: Tuten (ankle) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports.
items.analysis: If Tuten's absence Friday is confirmed by the team's injury report, that would mark a third consecutive 'DNP' for Jacksonville's starting running back. Coach Liam Coen intimated earlier Friday that Tuten's participation level Friday will factor into his potential availability for Sunday's game against the Titans, so he appears more likely than not to sit out Sunday based on this latest development. If Tuten is ruled out, Chris Rodriguez would be in line to lead a backfield that also includes LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah.

items.headline: Mitchell Evans (achilles) listed as questionable
items.news: Evans (Achilles) was a limited participant at practice Friday.
items.analysis: Evans took a step in the right direction by practicing to some extent Friday after being listed as non-participant on Thursday's estimate. He'll have one more chance to reach full participation Saturday ahead of Monday's game against the Buccaneers. Evans had his best game of 2026 in the Week 11 win over Baltimore, catching all five of his targets for 44 yards and his first touchdown of the season.

items.headline: Jonathon Brooks (groin) nearing return from IR
items.news: Brooks (groin) practiced without limitations Friday.
items.analysis: Brooks has shed any practice limitations, but he'll still need to be added back to the active roster to play Monday in Tampa Bay. Even if Brooks gets the green light to suit up and is activated by the Panthers, he'll likely have to settle for a change-of-pace role behind Chuba Hubbard against Tampa Bay's excellent run defense.

items.headline: Tommy Tremble (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Tremble (knee) remained a limited participant at practice Friday.
items.analysis: Tremble was limited again Friday after being listed a limited participant on Thursday's practice estimate. He has one more opportunity to upgrade to full participation Saturday, which could help Tremble avoid an injury designation for Monday's game against the Buccaneers.

items.headline: Juwan Johnson (hamstring) ruled out
items.news: Johnson (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Cincinnati, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Johnson suffered a hamstring injury this past Sunday at Chicago, and he then was listed as a DNP on the Saints' first two Week 12 practice reports, despite head coach Kellen Moore calling the tight end "day-to-day" Thursday, according to Terrell. With Johnson missing his first game of the campaign and Noah Fant (calf) questionable for Sunday's matchup, Oscar Delp is the sole healthy player at the position on the active roster.

items.headline: Jordan Addison (thumb) ruled out
items.news: Addison (thumb) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Dane Mizutani of the St. Paul Pioneer Press reports.
items.analysis: Addison thus will miss a third straight contest due to a thumb injury that required surgery. In Addison's continued absence, the Vikings will lean on Justin Jefferson, Jauan Jennings, Tai Felton, Myles Price and Jeshaun Jones at wide receiver. Addison's next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 6, versus the Panthers.

items.headline: Davis Allen (ankle) listed as out
items.news: Allen is dealing with a high-ankle sprain, according to sources, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.analysis: Allen was injured in the second quarter of Wednesday's win over the Packers. The Rams are still evaluating the extent of Allen's injury, but Rapoport mentions that high-ankle sprains are typically accompanied by recovery timelines of 4-to-6 weeks, so Allen is looking exceedingly unlikely to be available for the Rams' next game next Thursday against the Chiefs.

items.headline: Seth McGowan (hamstring) ruled out
items.news: McGowan (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants.
items.analysis: DJ Giddens is set to inherit change-of-pace duties behind Jonathan Taylor in McGowan's absence. McGowan, who injured his hamstring in the Week 11 loss to the Texans, will have a bye to heal before possibly returning against the Eagles in Week 14.

items.headline: Romeo Doubs (shoulder) remains on IR
items.news: Doubs (shoulder), who remains on injured reserve, has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
items.analysis: Since the Patriots designated Doubs for return from injured reserve Wednesday, he logged limited listings on injury reports. However, head coach Mike Vrabel told Evan Lazar of the team's official site Friday that Doubs is unlikely to play in Week 12, which now has been confirmed. Doubs will turn his sights to a Week 13 matchup with the Bills on Sunday, Dec. 6.

items.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) ruled out
items.news: Branch (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Minnesota, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
items.analysis: Branch will join Jahan Dotson (hamstring) on the sidelines in Week 12. Drake London, Olamide Zaccheaus, Beaux Collins and Chris Blair are Atlanta's available options at wide receiver, while Zaccheaus and Khalil Herbert are the top candidates to handle punt and kickoff returns in Branch's absence. Branch's next opportunity to suit up will be Sunday, Dec. 6, against Detroit.

items.headline: Jahan Dotson (hamstring) ruled out
items.news: Dotson (hamstring) wasn't spotted at practice Friday, Daniel Flick of the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
items.analysis: Dotson hasn't practiced all week, so it wouldn't be surprising if he's ultimately ruled out for Sunday's game against the Vikings once the Falcons release game designations Friday. Zachariah Branch (hamstring) also remained sidelined at Friday's practice, so Olamide Zaccheaus, Beaux Collins and Chris Blair may be Atlanta's only healthy and available wide receivers behind Drake London against Minnesota.

items.headline: Tyler Badie (thumb) injury update
items.news: Badie (thumb) is active Friday against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Badie was activated from injured reserve Thursday and will make his return Friday, likely working in a change-of-pace role behind Jonah Coleman while J.K. Dobbins is suspended. Cody Schrader also is on the roster at running back, while RJ Harvey (knee) could be activated from IR himself as soon as Week 13 against the Dolphins.

items.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) nearing return from IR
items.news: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Friday that he has no update on Love (ankle), who is eligible to come off injured reserve following Sunday's game against the Commanders, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
items.analysis: Love will miss a fourth consecutive game Sunday but will then be eligible to come off injured reserve ahead of Week 13 against the Eagles. LaFleur previously said Love will be reevaluated Monday once eligible to return, and the coach added Friday that he expects to know more Wednesday once the Cardinals return to practice. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight are still the leading in-house backfield options in the meantime.

items.headline: A.J. Brown (hamstring) ruled out
items.news: Brown (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
items.analysis: With Brown unavailable following the Patriots' Week 11 bye, Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams are in line to handle the team's WR duties in Tommy DeVito's first start of 2026. Meanwhile, Romeo Doubs (shoulder) isn't likely to be activated from IR this weekend, so it looks like the earliest either of New England's top two wideouts could be available is Sunday, Dec. 6, against the Bills.

items.headline: Colston Loveland (knee) listed as doubtful
items.news: Loveland (knee) is slated to get a second opinion on his knee injury and won't be placed on injured reserve for now, though he is considered week-to-week, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.analysis: Schefter reported earlier that the Bears planned to place Loveland on injured reserve due to the knee injury the TE sustained in Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions, which would rule Loveland out for at least four games. Chicago wants to gather more information before a determination is made on Loveland's status, and the door is still open for a shorter absence, though it would be surprising at this point if he's able to play Sunday, Dec. 6, against the Jaguars.

items.headline: Carson Beck (back) ruled out
items.news: Beck (back) will not play Sunday against the Commanders, coach Mike LaFleur said Friday, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Beck has yet to resume practicing and will miss a second consecutive game Sunday due to back spasms, paving the way for Josh Johnson to start against Washington. LaFleur added that a Week 13 return against the Eagles is in play for Beck, who made his first regular-season NFL start in a 34-6 Week 10 loss to the Rams. Beck's practice participation level leading up to that game will provide an indication regarding his potential availability, and LaFleur added that the team will know more about Beck's status "early in the week," per Weinfuss.

items.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) ruled out
items.news: Head coach Aaron Glenn announced Friday that Cooper (ankle/groin) will remain out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
items.analysis: Cooper will miss a second consecutive game Sunday, bringing him up to six total absences as a result of ankle injuries during his rookie campaign. Adonai Mitchell is set to start on the outside opposite Garrett Wilson, with Isaiah Williams manning the slot, though another elevation for practice-squad WR Sterling Shepard could be on the table after Shepard scored twice in the Week 11 win over the Chargers. Cooper's next chance to play will be a Week 14 home game against the Broncos following the Jets' Week 13 bye. Glenn said the timing of the bye played into the decision to keep Cooper out Sunday, per Rich Cimini of ESPN.com, which suggests Cooper has a decent chance to return after the bye.

items.headline: Parker Washington (shoulder) ruled out
items.news: Washington (shoulder) will be out for Sunday's game against the Titans and is considered week-to-week moving forward, Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports.
items.analysis: Washington was added to Jacksonville's injury report Thursday due to a shoulder injury, and the impact of the injury has escalated from limiting his practice participation Thursday to sidelining Jacksonville's top receiver Sunday and possibly beyond then. In Washington's absence, Jakobi Meyers (ankle), Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and possibly Travis Hunter or CJ Williams -- to a lesser degree -- could garner more attention from Trevor Lawrence against a Titans secondary that has allowed the most catches and yards per game in the league to wide receivers. Additional details regarding Washington's injury should emerge before the Jaguars travel to Chicago in Week 13.

items.headline: Jalen Royals (ankle) listed as questionable
items.news: Head coach Andy Reid said Royals suffered a sprained ankle during Thursday's 13-10 loss in Buffalo, Charles Goldman of AtoZSports.com reports.
items.analysis: Royals left the game in the third quarter and was ruled out not long afterward due to an ankle injury. The severity of the sprain will determine if Royals is in danger of missing any time. If that comes to pass for Royals, Andrew Armstrong likely will be on track for a few more offensive snaps behind Rashee Rice, Josh Downs, Xavier Worthy and Cyrus Allen.

items.headline: DeVonta Smith (back) listed as questionable
items.news: Smith (back) was seen limping badly in the locker room after Thursday's 39-38 win over the Cowboys, Martin Frank of the Delaware News Journal reports.
items.analysis: Smith put together a career stat line during the Eagles' Thanksgiving Day win, with the veteran wide receiver hauling in 11 of 14 targets for 200 yards and two touchdowns. He was in and out of the game after landing hard on his tailbone on one of his targets in the fourth quarter and was in noticeable pain when on the field. Smith will have additional time to rest courtesy of the Thursday game, but his status over the coming days will be worth monitoring ahead of the Eagles' Week 13 road tilt against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6.

items.headline: Dallas Goedert (shoulder) listed as questionable
items.news: Goedert (shoulder) had his right arm in a sling following Thursday's 39-38 victory over the Cowboys, Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.analysis: Goedert injured his right shoulder during the first half of Thursday's game and was not cleared to return. He'll undergo further tests to determine the severity of the injury, but the veteran tight end is certainly in jeopardy of not being available for the Eagles' Week 13 road tilt against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6. Johnny Mundt, Zach Ertz and rookie second-rounder Eli Stowers would all be in line for larger roles on offense if Goedert were to miss time.

items.headline: Saquon Barkley (neck) listed as questionable
items.news: Barkley suffered a stinger during Thursday's game in Dallas.
items.analysis: This marks Barkley's second diagnosed stinger of the campaign, but on the previous occasion in Week 2 against the Titans, he was able to check back in to the contest. The Eagles may opt to exercise caution with Barkley, however, because he tended to a neck issue on a short week following this past Sunday's win against the Steelers.

items.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) placed on IR
items.news: The Steelers placed Skowronek (calf) on injured reserve Thursday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
items.analysis: Skowronek has been working through a calf issue since mid-October, and he appeared to aggravate the injury during the Steelers' Week 11 loss to the Eagles. Now that he's on injured reserve, Skowronek will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 27. Max Hurleman was signed off the practice squad to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move.

items.headline: Caleb Lohner (foot) nearing return from IR
items.news: Lohner (foot) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Lohner was a full participant in all three practice sessions during Week 12 prep. However, the second-year pro is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve, so his next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6. Lohner is in the final stages of his recovery from a procedure on his foot in June.

items.headline: Christian Watson (concussion) listed as questionable
items.news: Watson (concussion) has been ruled out for the rest of Wednesday's game against the Rams.
items.analysis: The wideout hasn't cleared concussion checks and will miss the remainder of the Week 12 contest after he was injured at the end of the second quarter when Watson took a hit to the head from Kamren Kinchens. Look for J. Michael Sturdivant and Bo Melton to see increased snaps alongside Matthew Golden and Savion Williams with Watson sidelined.

items.headline: Dareke Young (stinger) practice update
items.news: Young (stinger) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Young was diagnosed with a stinger in the first half of the Raiders' 38-24 loss to the Broncos and did not return. However, his ability to practice in full Wednesday indicates that the fifth-year wide receiver will be available for Sunday's road game against the Browns. Young has mostly operated on special teams this season and has not been targeted in the passing game since Week 4 against the Chiefs.

items.headline: Josh Jacobs (finger) listed as out
items.news: Jacobs (finger) is listed as inactive Wednesday at the Rams, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
items.analysis: Coming out of the Packers' Week 11 bye, head coach Matt LaFleur told Matt Schneidman of The Athletic on Saturday that he didn't expect Jacobs to play in Week 12, but he also gave the running back a "chance to prove" he can. Jacobs then was listed as limited on practice reports Sunday through Tuesday and tagged as questionable ahead of Wednesday's game. Such activity wasn't enough for Jacobs to get the all clear to suit up, meaning Green Bay's backfield will be manned by Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks for a second consecutive contest.

items.headline: J.K. Dobbins (personal) suspended
items.news: The Broncos placed Dobbins on the reserve/suspended list Wednesday, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
items.analysis: Head coach Sean Payton had previously announced Tuesday that Dobbins would be suspended for Friday's game against the Steelers due to conduct detrimental to the team, but it wasn't immediately clear whether or not the running back would count toward the 53-man roster. As a result of Wednesday's transaction, the Broncos will now have an open roster spot to use for Week 12, and Tyler Badie (thumb) could be activated from injured reserve to help fill the void in the backfield. Dobbins' suspension came after he played just one snap in the Broncos' 38-24 win over the Raiders on Sunday, when rookie Jonah Coleman took on a bell-cow role and handled 28 touches.

items.headline: De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) nearing return from IR
items.news: San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan said Wednesday that Stribling (ankle) is likely at least "a couple weeks away" from returning to practice, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports. "I don't know. I mean, nothing's changed," Shanahan said, regarding a timeline for the rookie receiver.
items.analysis: Stribling was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle after getting injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and underwent surgery Sept. 16. The 23-year-old was handed an estimated recovery timeline of about 10 weeks, leaving the 49ers optimistic that he would be ready to play at some point in December. While Shanahan indicated that Stribling's timeline doesn't appear to have changed, the young wideout will need to get back on the practice field before the 49ers can hone in on a more precise target date for him to resume playing. Given the haziness of his return date along with the fact that he could face limitations with his snaps once activated, Stribling likely isn't worth holding in redraft leagues at this point in the season.

items.headline: Jake Ferguson (knee) injury update
items.news: The Cowboys ruled Ferguson (knee/ankle) out for Thursday's game against the Eagles, Patrik Walker of the team's official site reports.
items.analysis: As expected, Ferguson will be sidelined for a third straight game after he failed to practice in any fashion this week while continuing to tend to a pair of lower-body injuries. Brevyn Spann-Ford will be in line for another turn as the Cowboys' top tight end while Ferguson is sidelined. After the Thanksgiving Day contest, the Cowboys will face a longer turnaround for Week 13 with a Dec. 7 matchup against the Seahawks, and Ferguson should have decent odds of making it back for that game.

items.headline: Alec Pierce (heel) remains on IR
items.news: When addressing the press Wednesday, Pierce (heel) noted that the offseason procedure he underwent this past March was done because he was dealing with heel pain that impacted his Achilles, Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan Indianapolis reports.
items.analysis: Additionally, Pierce acknowledged that playing in Week 1 was a bit lofty, per Bowen, with the WR saying Wednesday that he was still managing some pain at that stage. In any case, Pierce indicated that he's confident that his current recovery plan will lead to a full return to health. When that will be remains to be seen, but the 2022 second-rounder is still on IR ahead of Week 12, with the Colts presumably not planning to rush him back given the team's 3-8 record in a campaign that's been marked by the team moving several key players ahead of the trade deadline.

items.headline: Kenneth Walker III (groin) ruled out
items.news: The Chiefs ruled out Walker (groin) for Thursday's game against the Bills.
items.analysis: Though Walker was able to log a limited practice Tuesday, he was listed as a non-participant Wednesday and will wind up missing a third straight contest while he continues to nurse a sore groin. With Walker sidelined, rookie Emmett Johnson is set for another turn as the Chiefs' lead back, with Jaydn Ott serving as his top backup and Nate Carter a possible practice-squad elevation. Given that the Chiefs on are on a short week, Walker -- who last saw game action Nov. 8 -- will have added time to heal before the team's next contest Dec. 3 against the Rams.

items.headline: Tanner McKee (ribs) practice update
items.news: McKee (ribs) was a full participant at the Eagles' walkthrough practice Tuesday.
items.analysis: McKee was estimated to be a limited participant on Monday's injury report due to an injury to his ribs. He now looks to be all set to serve as the team's primary reserve option at quarterback behind starter Joe Milton on Thursday against the Cowboys.

items.headline: Roschon Johnson (ankle) practice update
items.news: Johnson (ankle) was a nonparticipant at the Bears' walkthrough practice Tuesday.
items.analysis: Johnson was considered unavailable for practice for a second straight day as he continues to nurse an ankle injury he suffered in Week 11 against the Saints. If the running back is unable to play Thursday versus the Lions, Salvon Ahmed would be a top candidate to be elevated from the practice squad for a second week in a row.

items.headline: Jonathan Mingo (ankle) practice update
items.news: Mingo (ankle) did not participate in practice Tuesday.
items.analysis: Mingo downgraded from his limited participation in Monday's practice to full DNP Tuesday. The 25-year-old missed the last two games due to an ankle injury and could be in danger of missing Thursday's divisional game against the Eagles if he doesn't upgrade his practice status Wednesday. KaVontae Turpin and Camden Brown have been rotational options at wide receiver in Mingo's absence.

items.headline: Ben VanSumeren (knee) injury update
items.news: The Chiefs placed VanSumeren (knee) on the reserve/injured list Tuesday.
items.analysis: VanSumeren didn't practice Tuesday due to a sprained knee that will now keep him out for at least the next four weeks, according to Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site. In six regular-season games in 2026, the fourth-year pro played a majority of his reps on special teams, with just six of 104 total snaps coming on offense.

items.headline: George Holani (knee) placed on IR
items.news: The Seahawks placed Holani (knee) on injured reserve Monday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
items.analysis: Holani was knocked out of the Seahawks' last game in Week 10 at Las Vegas due to a knee injury that eventually was deemed to be an MCL sprain. Per Brady Henderson of ESPN.com, head coach Mike Macdonald said he was uncertain if Holani will require surgery, but the running back will be sidelined for at least four games by virtue of landing on IR. In the meantime, Emanuel Wilson will serve as the team's No. 3 back behind Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price.

items.headline: Drake Maye (ankle) listed as out
items.news: For now, Maye -- who suffered a fractured right fibula during a Week 10 loss to the Lions -- remains on the Patriots' 53-man roster rather than injured reserve, with coach Mike Vrabel citing the "balance" the team is hoping to strike with regard to managing its remaining designated to return from IR slots, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Per Reiss, teams are limited to eight players that can be designated to return from the list over the course of the regular season, and the Patriots are close to using them all. "Right now, he's not on injured reserve," Vrabel said Monday. "He's on the active roster, so that's where it is today. I think that those things are obviously fluid. But we want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time. I don't know when that will be; I'm not sure. But also, try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week." On Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Maye was on track to miss at least six weeks, a timetable that suggests, in a best-case scenario, the QB could make a push for a late-season return or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Heading into a Week 12 game against the Chargers, Tommy DeVito is slated to work as the team's starter, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup. Additionally, there's the possibility that the team considers Daniel Jones -- who the Colts let go Friday -- as an alternative, but Vrabel told Reiss that in the short term at least, adding another signal-caller is not something that's being planned.

items.headline: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) activated
items.news: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Monday that Ferguson (hamstring) won't be activated from injured reserve this season and will require surgery to address the ankle injury he aggravated in Week 3, Stu Jackson of the team's official site reports.
items.analysis: Ferguson initially seemed to be making good progress in his recovery from the ankle injury, as the Rams elected to open his 21-day evaluation window Nov. 4. However, Ferguson's activation from IR was delayed after he strained his hamstring shortly after he resumed working out, and he hasn't practiced in more than two weeks. Rather than the hamstring issue, McVay noted that the ankle injury remained the greater concern for Ferguson, who didn't improve as well as the Rams had hoped and now will require a procedure. Los Angeles will have to proceed without two of its top pass catchers for the remainder of the season, as Puka Nacua recently underwent an MCL surgery that entails an estimated 4-to-5-month recovery timeline.

items.headline: Malik Willis (groin) remains on IR
items.news: Head coach Jeff Hafley said Monday that, at this time, surgery to address Willis' groin/core injury is not foreseen, Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post reports.
items.analysis: That said, per Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com, Hafley added that the Dolphins will evaluate the QB's status again depending on how he feels at the end of his minimum required stay on IR. For now, Willis is out for at least three more games, with Kyle McCord currently filling in as 1-9 Miami's starting signal-caller.

items.headline: RJ Harvey (knee) remains on IR
items.news: Harvey is on injured reserve with a knee injury.

items.headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist) injury update
items.news: Hockenson (wrist) caught six of seven targets for 55 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
items.analysis: In his return from a one-game absence, Hockenson finished second on the team in receiving yards behind Justin Jefferson's 86. Hockenson showed promising chemistry with Kirk Cousins after the veteran TE sat out Cousins' return to Minnesota during the Week 10 win over Green Bay. Cousins was under center for the Vikings in the 2023 regular season, when Hockenson set career highs with 95 catches for 960 yards. Hockenson hasn't surpassed 455 yards in a regular season since, though he's on pace to do so this year, with 41 catches for 383 yards and three touchdowns through nine appearances heading into a Week 12 home game against the Falcons.

items.headline: Luke Musgrave (neck) listed as out
items.news: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Saturday that he doesn't anticipate Musgrove (neck) returning from the PUP list this season, according to NFL reporter Jason B. Hirschhorn.
items.analysis: LaFleur acknowledged that Musgrove is still in the process of rehabbing the neck injury he sustained during OTAs in June, and the Packers haven't yet prepared for the tight end to resume practicing. Barring dramatic progress in his recovery over the next month, Musgrave looks like he'll be sidelined for the final season of his rookie deal before hitting free agency in the spring.

items.headline: Jeshaun Jones (shoulder) injury update
items.news: Jones (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.
items.analysis: Jones -- who was managing a shoulder injury during Week 11 prep -- was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He was signed to the Vikings' 53-man roster Wednesday to give the team more depth at wide receiver while Jordan Addison recovers from a thumb injury. Jones figures to be limited to a rotational role on offense while serving as a contributor on special teams.

items.headline: Puka Nacua (MCL) remains on IR
items.news: Nacua (knee/toe) is expected to be sidelined 4-to-5 months after undergoing surgery Tuesday to repair his right MCL, which means he won't be on track to return at any point during the playoffs, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.analysis: Nacua is also dealing with a PCL sprain and turf toe, but the only procedure he required was for his MCL. With a firmer 4-to-5-month timeline now in place for the star wideout, he'll be done for the season while the Rams look to others to help fill the massive void in their receiver corps. Davante Adams (hamstring) should eventually take on a heavy target share, but he's also on injured reserve and isn't expected to return until at least Week 13. That leaves Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith as the current healthy wideouts on the team's 53-man roster ahead of next Wednesday's tilt versus the Packers. Nacua, who is in the final year of his rookie deal, is slated to become a free agent in March.

items.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) placed on IR
items.news: The Eagles placed Wicks (ankle/foot) on injured reserve Saturday.
items.analysis: Wicks missed the three games before the Eagles' Week 10 bye due to an ankle injury, and he was limited during Week 11 prep before the team tacked on a foot issue on Friday's practice report, after which he was ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Steelers. Per Tim McManus of ESPN.com, Wicks sustained the foot injury Friday, and it presumably led to his placement on IR. Wicks will be sidelined until at least Philadelphia's Week 15 matchup with Seattle on Saturday, Dec. 19.

items.headline: Colson Yankoff (knee) practice update
items.news: Yankoff (knee) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Yankoff sat out the Commanders' contest against the Giants in Week 10 because of a knee injury, but it now looks like he's put it behind him. He figures to resume a depth role at tight end in Week 11 against the Bengals.
